title: Why Is Mexico Defying Latin America’s Right Turn?
gist: Paywalled teaser: Viri Ríos argues Mexico's ruling left-wing Morena party bucks Latin America's right turn thanks to pragmatic politics combining bold redistribution, greater security and willingness to compromise; Morena is expected to win five times the votes of any opposition party in next year's legislative elections.

themes.theme: Morena's pragmatic left versus Latin America's right turn

insights.claim: With much of Latin America drawn to the radical right, Brazil and Mexico have emerged as the region's last major bastions of left-wing government.
insights.speaker: Viri Ríos
insights.so_what: Regional political drift to the right leaves Mexico and Brazil as policy outliers worth tracking for investors in LatAm.
insights.quote: Brazil and Mexico have emerged as the region’s last major bastions of left-wing government
insights.locator: MEXICO CITY—With much of Latin America

insights.claim: Mexico's ruling Morena party is expected to win five times as many votes as any opposition party in next year's legislative elections, whereas Brazil's Lula faced an uphill battle to win re-election.
insights.speaker: Viri Ríos
insights.so_what: Expect policy continuity in Mexico with a dominant ruling party and weak opposition.
insights.quote: is expected to win five times as many votes as any opposition party in next year’s legislative elections
insights.locator: MEXICO CITY—With much of Latin America

insights.claim: Morena's sustained support most likely stems from a pragmatic left-wing brand combining bold redistributive policies, greater security and a willingness to compromise in the name of both.
insights.speaker: Viri Ríos
insights.so_what: Mexican policy mix likely to keep pairing redistribution with security spending rather than radical shifts.
insights.quote: combines bold redistributive policies, greater security, and a willingness to compromise in the name of both
